This document covers the water 
treatment plant of Ayoun 
Moussa PS.

The wastewater system collects wastewater from power station in various sumps 
for treatment. The wastewater is neutralized and treated, then discharged back 
to the Red Sea via the seal well in the circulating water discharge (DA).

(PLC) is an automatic programmable logic 
controller system.

The water treatment properties will comply 
with the requirement of Egyptian Law number (4) for year 1994.

sections.text: The major components of the wastewater system are:

Waste Neutralization Tank
The 
neutralization tank accepts chemical cleaning waste and potentially chemical 
based waste from the condensate polisher area sumps and the demineralizer system 
waste sump. The contents are neutralized to a pH level of 6-9 with the addition 
of sulfuric acid (H2SO4) and caustic (sodium hydroxide NaOH). The level 
switches in the tank, and pH analyzers in the re-circulation line; provide 
signals to the makeup demineralizer control panel, AN-CP01, which uses the 
signal in the demineralizer PLC for the waste neutralization transfer 
pumps, 
chemical metering pump controls, and local tank level indication and alarms.

Waste Neutralization Transfer Pump
 Each waste neutralization transfer pump is 
a 100% capacity pump sized to discharge the contents of a level-full waste 
neutralizing tank in approximately 5 hours.

Equalization Basin
All waste fluids are 
collected in the equalization basin and mixed thoroughly with two submersible 
mixers.

Waste Collection Area 
The waste collection area 
consists of a pre-mix section with floating mixers, two collection basins and a 
clear well section. Acid and caustic are supplied as required for further 
neutralization, and coagulant and coagulant aid are added to the premix section.

Vertical Sump Pumps
Sump pumps in the wastewater 
system are vertical submerged type pumps. The pumps are manufactured by Ingersoll-Dresser. The pumps are driven by 400 Vac electric motors. All sumps 
have two 100% pumps (one leading and one lagging). The controls for a sump pump consist of a local 
hand switch and a ball float type level switch mounted on the base plate (sump 
cover) for operation. The level control provides a 
signal to the pump alternator panel, which will start pumps singly in an 
alternate sequence. If the scheduled pump fails to start, the alternate pump 
will receive a signal to start. If load demands, both pumps will start. The circulating water pump-house sump pumps are the only exception 
to this control 
philosophy. Both pumps feed the oil/water coalescer and will never operate 
simultaneously.

Coalescer Type Oil/Water Separator
The coalescer type oil/water 
separator in the circulating water pump-house area, is sized to process 200 lpm 
of oily wastes. The flow capacity of the separator is based on a maximum of one 
sump pump. The oil/water separator uses coalescing media to separate the oil 
from the water and then stores the separated oil in an integral oil storage 
tank. The oil is then pumped to a truck or drums for disposal off-site.

sections.text:
Verify that all sump pumps hand switches are in the AUTO position so that 
the sump pumps respond to sump level signals.

Pumps start and stop in response to level signals to maintain tank and 
sump levels. Where two pumps are installed in one sump, the pumps automatically 
alternate in operation each time one starts/stops to equalize run time.

During regeneration or a high waste tank level condition, one waste 
neutralization pump runs continuously, recirculating the water in the waste 
neutralization tank through the recycle valve.

The sump pumps are not normally shut down (hand switch in the OFF 
position) except for maintenance. Otherwise, they are allowed to cycle as the 
sump level requires.

Before shutting down all pumps operating in a sump, ensure that the sumps 
or equipment discharging to that sump will not require the sump's operation 
during the shutdown period.

The accumulation of solid waste in the active collection basin will 
eventually need to be removed. Open the path to the alternate premix section 
and close the path leading to the active basin. Allow enough time for the water 
in the basin to drain into the clear well. Proceed with sludge removal as per the 
plant procedures.

The sumps receive water from equipment and floor drains. The water is 
pumped first to the parallel plate oil/water separator (9LE-F002) where the 
first stage of oil removal takes place. The effluent then flows to the air 
floatation type oil/water separator (9LE‑F001) for final processing.

The following sump pumps deliver wastewater to the air floatation type 
oil/water separator:

Wastewater is separated from oily wastes and then discharged to the 
wastewater equalization basin.

The circulating water pump house sumps discharge to the coalescer 
oil/water separator where the collected oil is stored for off-site disposal and 
the water is discharged back to the sea via the screen wash system trash basket.

Waste neutralization tank (9-LG-T001) collects wastewater from the water 
treatment building chemical drain sump and the condensate polisher area sumps.

On a high level signal in the neutralization tank, regeneration of a 
demineralizer train is interrupted (if in progress), and the contents of the 
tank are neutralized, then discharged until a low level signal from the tank is 
achieved.

Waste neutralization is controlled locally at makeup demineralizer 
control panel (AN‑CP001). Normally, waste neutralization is left in automatic, 
controlled by the PLC. The operator can control the system manually, through 
the PLC, at the local console.

After the regeneration of a demineralizer train, or any time a high level 
is reached in the neutralization tank, the PLC starts a waste neutralization 
transfer pump to recirculate tank contents. The pump takes suction from the 
tank and discharges the fluid to a common pump discharge header. An effluent 
sample line is provided at the pump discharge header to route sample fluid to a 
pH analyzer and back to the tank. The pump discharges the fluid through a 
recycle valve and a recirculating line into the waste neutralization tank 
recirculation header. Two educators are used at the recirculation header to 
promote thorough mixing in the tank.

During recirculation mode, the pH analyzer will continuously check the 
fluid and send a pH signal to the PLC. If the pH is within 6.0 to 9.0 (the 
optimum range for discharge), a dump valve opens and the wastewater is pumped to 
the equalization basin until a low level is reached in the waste neutralization 
tank. If the pH is not within the proper range, the neutralization system 
enters an acid or caustic injection mode and the contents continue to be 
recirculated.

In the injection mode, an acid or caustic feed pump will be started and 
the appropriate acid or caustic block valve will open. This will admit acid or 
caustic to the appropriate mixing tee as the tank contents are being 
recirculated. The acid and caustic block valves are controlled by the PLC.

At the end of the injection mode, the appropriate metering pump is shut 
down and the block valve is closed. The neutralization system then re-enters 
the mixing mode.

After the tank contents have been mixed for the appropriate amount of 
time, the pH is again checked. If the pH is acceptable, the pump valve will be 
opened, the recycle valve closed, and the contents of the tank discharged. If 
the pH is unacceptable or the pH goes out of range during the pump mode, the 
injection and mixing process will be repeated until the pH is acceptable and the 
tank contents discharged.

At the completion of regeneration or whenever the tank is full, and in 
both cases after an appropriate mixing time has elapsed, the pH will be checked.

If a high level is reached in the tank before a regeneration is 
completed, the regeneration will be halted and the neutralization cycle 
performed before the regeneration will be resumed.

The wastewater is collected in the wastewater equalization 
basin where it is mixed thoroughly by submersible mixers and then pumped to one 
of two premix sections in the waste collection area.

In the premix section, waste may be neutralized with sulfuric 
acid and sodium hydroxide. Sodium hypochlorite (NaOCI) is injected 
in the premix section to control biological growth. The addition of coagulant 
and a coagulant aid, along with the action of the floating mixers, help 
suspended solids coalesce into larger particles to allow rapid settling basins. 
The metering pumps injecting the coagulant and a coagulant aid are 
controlled by the water treatment PLC, which receives a signal from a flow 
meter downstream of the equalization basin.

The clear well transfer pumps discharge the clear effluent 
through the pressure sand filters and then to the circulating water seal well 
and on to the Red Sea. The pH is continuously monitored and if it exceeds 
the acceptable limits, it is sent back to the equalization basin.

The solid waste collected must be periodically cleaned out of 
the collection basin and transported off site for disposal.

The demineralize system supplies acid and caustic to the day tanks 
water premix section for pH control in the waste neutralization tank and the 
waste.

The circulating water discharge seal well accepts the treated waste water 
and discharges it to the sea.

The sodium hypochlorite injection system supplies sodium hypochlorite in 
the premix section to control biological growth.

The compressed air system provides clean, dry air to operate valves and 
controllers within the wastewater system.

The low voltage (400 V) 
distribution system provides power for the pumps, mixers, and other equipments.

Directives
Oily Wastewater

Turbine area for units 1 and 2
Boiler area for units 1 and 2

wastewater equalization basin.
